title: Pharma 4.0 and the Evolution of Quality by Design: Integrating Process Analytics, Artificial Intelligence, and Digital Twins
content: Background: Pharma 4.0 integrates Quality by Design (QbD) with digital technologies to strengthen pharmaceutical process understanding, monitoring, and control. However, the extent to which these technologies support validated, adaptive manufacturing systems remains uncertain. This review assesses their relationship with QbD elements, implementation scale, evidence maturity, and regulatory considerations. Methods: A structured narrative review of scientific literature, regulatory guidance, and standards was undertaken using a literature-identification and selection process informed by PRISMA 2020. Evidence was synthesized qualitatively across process analytical technology (PAT), the industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML), and digital twins. Results: Evidence maturity differed across the four domains. PAT applications were reported across pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical operations, including pilot-scale settings. IIoT evidence primarily supported connectivity and monitoring, while end-to-end validated data-integrity architectures were less well established in the reviewed sources. AI/ML evidence ranged from laboratory modelling to a reported study evaluating ANN-derived limits using GMP exhibit batches, with bioequivalence reported. Direct evidence for digital twins supporting pharmaceutical process decisions remained limited, and many applications were conceptual or at an early stage. Conclusions: QbD 4.0 should be advanced through reliable data infrastructure, fit-for-purpose validation, lifecycle governance, cybersecurity, controlled change management, and human oversight. A staged, evidence-based approach is needed; monitoring or predictive performance alone does not establish validated process control or regulatory acceptability.
